sections.text: Semantic HTML vs Div Soup

HTML provides structural meaning to web documents. Semantic elements like <header>, <main>, <nav>, and <article> communicate role and hierarchy to browser engines, assistive technologies (screen readers), and search indexers.
Using a <button> instead of a <div onClick> gives you keyboard accessibility (Enter/Space triggers) and focus management for free without writing custom event handlers.

sections.text: Understanding box-sizing: border-box

Every element on a web page is represented as a rectangular box comprising content, padding, border, and margin. In default content-box sizing, padding and border ADD to the element's specified width, breaking layouts unexpectedly.

sections.label: I know why border-box is essential for predictable layout math.
sections.hint: border-box includes padding and border inside the specified width and height.

sections.title: Box Sizing Comparison Sandbox

quiz.question: What happens when box-sizing is set to border-box?
options: Padding is added outside the element width
Padding and border are included inside the element width
quiz.explanation: border-box ensures the specified width includes content, padding, and border.

summary: The box model dictates sizing math, while specificity controls which rules win when selectors compete.
interviewQuestions: Explain the difference between content-box and border-box.

sections.text: The Temporal Dead Zone (TDZ)
let and const variables are hoisted to the top of their block scope, but remain uninitialized in the TDZ until execution reaches their declaration.

summary: Block scoping with let/const prevents variable leaks and enforces disciplined declaration timing.

A closure is a function bundled together with references to its surrounding state — the lexical environment in which it was declared.

sections.text: Promise States & Chaining
A Promise is an object representing eventual completion or failure of an async operation. It resides in one of three states: pending, fulfilled, or rejected.

summary: Promises replace callback hell with structured async task composition.

sections.text: Microtasks vs Macrotasks
Microtasks (Promises, queueMicrotask) run immediately after the current call stack clears, before macrotasks (setTimeout) or browser repaints.

summary: Microtasks drain completely before the event loop advances to the next task.
